correctedFields.moveProse.con-gospels-mythic-literary-ma: Strongest feature: The argument concedes literary shaping does not erase every historical element, while identifying the methodological difficulty of extracting secure resurrection history from narratives containing proposed borrowing and mythic construction. Principal limitation: Calling the Gospels riddled with myth outruns the limited parallel evidence, and neither establishes that relevant resurrection traditions were invented nor demonstrates that distinct Pauline testimony shares the alleged defect. Live burden: O'Connor must distinguish dependence, typology, shared motifs, and direct borrowing, then connect demonstrated literary construction to the particular appearance claims bearing the central historical burden. Locked score: The strong band reflects substantial source-level relevance, an important concession, and meaningful contact with Gospel-based evidence, while retaining reservations concerning generalized terminology and unanswered early testimony.
correctedFields.moveProse.pro-exodus-injury-protection.c: Strongest feature: McLatchie introduces the adjacent eye-and-tooth release provisions, providing textual evidence that bodily injury could carry legal consequences and complicating claims that abusive treatment was wholly unrestricted. Principal limitation: Extrapolation from specified injuries to a comprehensive rule remains unestablished, while even broader release would not explain why the survival provision withholds punishment in serious cases beneath the asserted threshold. Live burden: McLatchie must justify the provisions' legal scope, reconcile them with the preceding beating rule, and address whether regulation and release are morally adequate under claimed divine perfection. Locked score: The strong band reflects concrete evidence and substantial contact with a central objection, tempered by overextended scope, incomplete statutory reconciliation, and insufficient engagement with the surviving-victim case.
